title: Identify the finite-category lifting tests
as_he_states: RLP against the displayed sphere/interval family implies W∞-asphericity; cone and finite-immersion variants imply properness/smoothness and an undefined perfectness property.
plausible_today: A functor lifting against every full inclusion of finite categories that is a nerve weak equivalence is proper and smooth. This does not identify the displayed sphere family or “parfait”.
state_of_art: Thomason1980 Propositions2.5–2.6 distinguish horn and boundary tests. Cisinski2006 §5.3.12/Proposition5.3.13 proves the modern full-inclusion variant via its finite proper/smooth horn families. Maltsiniotis2005 Theorem1.2 and Proposition4.3 give precise target properties.
why_open: No explanation is supplied; this leaf gives no proof and has overwritten qualifiers. Unreadable definitions, rather than absence of modern theory, prevent exact identification.
worth: Worth a short scan-based reconstruction, since one qualifier changes the theorem and an exact modern comparison is available.

title: Is retract stability of W redundant?
as_he_states: If the two pairs are Quillen pairs, should it be unnecessary to assume direct-factor stability of W? The later page doubts the implication for W but says Quillen proves strong saturation, at least with finite direct and inverse limits. Additional occurrence/formulation: Is stability under direct factors already a consequence of saturation?
plausible_today: With Quillen's model axioms including finite (co)limits, closedness yields W=γ^-1(Iso), hence arrow-retract stability. Under only a relative category, special split saturation, cyclic saturation and arrow-retract closure must be distinguished. A statement without M0 must explicitly replace the missing structure. Additional occurrence/formulation: State the exact saturation convention and categorical structure. Full model-category hypotheses give arrow-retract closure and localization saturation; the initial split-retraction axiom alone is not here promoted to all arrow retracts.
state_of_art: Quillen1967 I§5 Propositions1–2 (LR-B-01) settles the qualified model-category question already at the time. RadulescuBanu2006 Theorem7.2.7 (LR-B-10) gives a later equivalence under precofibration or prefibration hypotheses. Neither is a theorem about every arbitrary category with two arrow-factorization systems and no further specified structure. Additional occurrence/formulation: Quillen1967 I§5 Propositions1–2 proves the model-category conclusions. GrothendieckPS1983 §48 separately distinguishes cyclic saturation. The cyclic-composite question is separately indexed as MP-SA25-32, and the bare-arrow-data question as MP-SA25-37.
why_open: The text explicitly identifies its uncertainty and cites Quillen rather than completing a proof. No external source consulted explains why this particular working note was left unfinished. Additional occurrence/formulation: The same manuscript repeatedly questions the conventions. No reason for historical neglect is inferred.
worth: Worth a short axiom-dependency audit that separates the proved model-category theorem from the weaker initial convention, while leaving the cyclic and no-finite-(co)limits questions in their separate records.

title: Do two weak cyclic composites force both factors weak?
as_he_states: Assuming Iso⊂W, two-of-three, and closure under retracts, ask whether fg,gf∈W implies f,g∈W. The sheet separately draws the implications from this cyclic condition and from retract closure to the special split condition.
plausible_today: The displayed general implication is false. It becomes true when W is strongly saturated, or under the structured saturation hypotheses in LR-B-10. The special split condition gf=id,fg∈W⇒f,g∈W is weaker than the cyclic condition in an arbitrary category.
state_of_art: The full N/even counterexample and refined statement RF-SA25-106 are independently proved in proofs.md. The literature search found the exact structured equivalence RadulescuBanu2006 Theorem7.2.7, not a generic equivalence. No priority claim is made for the counterexample.
why_open: There is no account of abandonment beyond cancellation of the entire sheet. The later scan28 returns to the model-category context and cites the stronger Quillen theorem.
worth: Closed as a generic mathematical question by the checked counterexample; retain it as a useful warning about hypothesis changes.

title: Properness for a prescribed cohomological localizer
as_he_states: The extra property is particularly important: W should survive pullback along the selected F and pushout along C. His intended W is given by cohomological criteria; the text does not name one definitive coefficient/localizer choice here.
plausible_today: For an accessible localizer on a Grothendieck topos with C the monomorphisms, the associated model structure is left proper. Right properness requires the exact generator pullback criterion in LR-B-08. It is not obtained merely by defining F through a lifting property.
state_of_art: Cisinski2002 Theorem3.9, Remark4.4 and Theorem4.8 (LR-B-08) establish this precise conditional answer. The theorem tests each generator X→Y after every map Y→B and every fibration E→B with fibrant B. The manuscript has not supplied such a set of generators for its unspecified cohomological W.

worth: Worth a focused run only after selecting a concrete W and coefficients; the first task is to test its generators against the exact right-properness criterion.

title: Saturation from bare arrow data without finite (co)limits
as_he_states: The marginal qualification 'at any rate if ... finite direct and inverse limits exist (M0)' leaves the broader implication from the two Quillen pairs to W retract stability and strong saturation unproved. Keep it separate from the settled model-category case.
plausible_today: With finite limits and colimits the answer is positive (MP-SA25-31). For arrow-retract closure alone, inspection of the checked Joyal–Tierney/Riehl argument shows it suffices to have the pushouts of trivial cofibrations along the split inclusions arising in arrow-retract diagrams. That is this run's hypothesis analysis, not their theorem's written formulation. Strong saturation without all relevant structural assumptions is not inferred.
state_of_art: Quillen1967 I§5 Propositions1–2 give the finite-(co)limit result. JoyalTierney2008 AppendixA PropositionA.3.1 and Riehl2014 Lemma11.3.3 (LR-B-13,14) prove W retract closure using two weak factorization systems plus two-of-three and a pushout. RadulescuBanu2006 Theorem7.2.7 supplies another precise structured generalization. The recorded search did not locate an exact theorem or counterexample for completely bare nonfunctorial arrow data without those constructions; this is a bounded search result, not a claim of present mathematical openness.
why_open: The source itself qualifies the assertion by M0 and records doubt. No explanation of a later abandonment was found; it must not be folded into the known Quillen theorem.
worth: A focused foundations run could isolate the genuinely minimal limits/functoriality assumptions and search the exact bare formulation; the first step is to state the arrow-data axioms without importing M0.

title: Can the lifting class be closed under arbitrary filtering limits?
as_he_states: After setting Φ=Ψ*, he asks whether conditiond follows and sketches a Zorn argument on partial compatible lifts; a margin allows a directed poset with binary suprema.
plausible_today: Continuous ordinal composites of left lifting maps have the lifting property. Arbitrary directed diagrams need additional hypotheses beyond LLP of all transition maps.
state_of_art: Cisinski2006 Remark1.2.20 verifies the ordinal closure. P1 independently refutes the stronger claim in Ab using finite-rank pure subgroups of Z^N, with the nonfree premise checked in Schroer2007. The exact directedness and all transition-map hypotheses are proved.
why_open: The scan38 argument breaks off; scan40 writes continuity and ordinal indexing explicitly. No source records a historical reason for that narrowing.
worth: Worth an editorial resolution of the two distinct statements; the unrestricted mathematical question is already negatively decided by the checked counterexample.

title: The heading W equals W_D
as_he_states: The new section is headed “Dém. de W7, W(7bis) et W=W_D ?”. No complete equality theorem with all hypotheses is stated in this fragment.
plausible_today: For a specified derivator D on Cat, define W_D by constant-coefficient cohomology equivalence. Under the usual axioms it is a fundamental localizer and contains W∞. Equality with an independently chosen W needs a representation/detection theorem for that W, not only square exactness.
state_of_art: Cisinski2008 Definition3.2, Proposition3.7 and Corollary3.10 give exactly those basic properties; Corollary3.5 identifies W_Hot with W∞. These do not prove arbitrary W=W_D. No exact theorem can be identified from the heading without its missing hypotheses.

worth: Worth reconstructing the precise coefficient-detection definition from the surrounding author corpus before formulating a new representability question.

title: Reverse edge isomorphisms and reverse excision
as_he_states: The opposite-edge isomorphism equivalence is “à vérifier” or to be made an axiom; the reverse W_D implication is then tied to cocartesianness of the coherent square.
plausible_today: For coherent bicartesian squares both opposite-edge tests hold; a cartesian square alone provides only the pullback direction. A stable coefficient derivator makes the cohomology square bicartesian when the right-Kan construction applies.
state_of_art: Groth2013 Proposition3.13 and Proposition4.5 verify the exact coherent edge criteria. The unrestricted W∞ reverse statement fails, as shown by P8; this does not disprove a stronger coefficient-localizer axiom.
why_open: The pages themselves identify the missing cocartesian property; no further historical cause is documented.
worth: Worth presenting the conditional proof and the exact point where a proposed extra axiom enters, since this prevents a mistaken universal W∞ theorem.

title: How far may the coefficient quantifier be enlarged?
as_he_states: One margin allows every ξ∈D(barX|X), a locally constant clause is cancelled, and a later margin asks whether non-locally-constant ξ already makes the proposal false.
plausible_today: The coherent right-Kan square is cartesian for arbitrary coefficients on its total category. Transfer between barX and X requires correctly transported coefficients, e.g. p*η, or a suitable local-system hypothesis. Cocartesianness needs extra stable/exactness assumptions even for constant coefficients.
state_of_art: Cisinski2008 Lemma2.3 establishes the right-Kan calculation; Cegarra2020 §1 distinguishes weak-equivalence invariance from arbitrary-coefficient cohomology. P4 gives the exact 4-versus1 counterexample and p*η repair; P5 shows that constant coefficients do not rescue Der6 in spaces.
why_open: The author visibly changes and questions coefficient scope. The unavailable ink prevents choosing barX versusX; no psychological explanation is inferred.
worth: High-value next scan check: the coefficient domain changes the theorem, and the present run already supplies the alternatives that the ink must decide.

title: Do the provisional Der6 and Der6-prime follow from earlier axioms?
as_he_states: The author suspects the extra cocartesian property cannot follow from Der1–5,5′, writes provisional cofibration/fibration axioms, and questions their scope.
plausible_today: Both proposals hold for stable derivators with coherent diagrams and matched variance. Neither follows for arbitrary derivators: P5 gives counterexamples in spaces satisfying even the constant-coefficient subcases.
state_of_art: Groth2013 Definition4.1 and GrothPontoShulman2014 Theorem7.1 give precise stable criteria. The explicit opfibred and fibred examples in P5 verify the missing implication without relying on a vague analogy with stability.
why_open: The text itself replaces the provisional forms by the stronger geometric axiom on50. The later theory explains a valid scope, but no source says this is why the author made the change.
worth: Worth a concise historical commentary separating the two provisional forms from the later stability criterion; no new theorem is required for these counterexamples.

title: An internal dualizing functor relating cohomology and homology
as_he_states: He sees no implication between the dual proposals except possibly when there is a dualizing functor on A=D(e) and a duality correspondence between homology and cohomology.
plausible_today: Opposition of the whole derivator always exchanges left/right and cartesian/cocartesian after indexing variance is reversed. A duality within the same coefficient theory needs a specified exact duality functor, its domain and compatibility with Kan extension; no universal such functor is expected from the stated axioms.
state_of_art: Groth2013 Definition1.15, Example1.16 and Example4.2 verify opposite-derivator formalism. Searches found no exact theorem matching the unspecified internal functor on this page. External project claims about kernels, finite-category duality or ambidexterity were not supplied and remain unchecked leads.
why_open: The page calls the situation exceptional and gives no construction; no source records a reason for not pursuing it.
worth: Worth formulating only after choosing a concrete coefficient category and finiteness conditions, because the manuscript does not determine a single duality problem.

title: The geometric square axiom, including all shifts
as_he_states: Every coherent square should be cartesian iff cocartesian, “à moins que ça ne soit absurde”; impose the test also for each induced D_I.
plausible_today: A pointed derivator with this square property is stable; all shifts of a stable derivator are stable. The page's unpointed proposal should be reported as the square property rather than silently given all modern stable hypotheses.
state_of_art: Groth2013 Definition4.1/Proposition4.3 and GrothPontoShulman2014 Theorem7.1 identify the precise conditions and shift theorem.
why_open: The hesitation is explicit; the supplied pages do not decide the admissible coefficient theories.
worth: Worth a precise terminology comparison with modern stability, especially the absent pointedness assumption, rather than treating this as an unresolved universal axiom.

title: The collapse lemma and the doubtful properness of rho
as_he_states: To collapse the isomorphic leg, prove the counit ρ*ρ_*ξ→ξ is an isomorphism; the proof callsρ smooth and perhaps proper, and invokes locally constant interval diagrams.
plausible_today: For the stated isomorphism leg, pointwise Kan calculation proves the counit is invertible. The functorρ is not universally proper in presheaf right-Kan variance; the fibrewise formula needs the isomorphism hypothesis here.
state_of_art: Groth2013 Proposition3.13 verifies the interval-isomorphism essential image. Cisinski2008 Lemma2.3 and Maltsiniotis2005 Definition1.1 locate the proper/smooth distinction. P5 computes the correct counit and a 4-versus2 failure of unconditional fibrewise right Kan extension.
why_open: The word proper is marked uncertain in the transcription; only the scan can decide whether this is an ink issue or a mathematical overstatement.
worth: Worth a targeted scan and proof annotation, since the lemma is sound while one possible justification is not.

title: The marginal contractibility criterion after the Hot withdrawal
as_he_states: After withdrawing the universal Hot claims, the margin asks whether a bicartesian square ending in e forces one adjacent object to be contractible.
plausible_today: For a cartesian product square ending in a point, cocartesianness means that the join of the two adjacent spaces is contractible. This need not make either factor contractible.
state_of_art: P6 supplies an explicit acyclic noncontractible finite CW complexK and proves K*K contractible; its boundary and nontrivial group quotient are exactly certified. Hatcher2002 Theorem2.35 and Corollary4.33 are the checked topological tools.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly retracts the preceding paragraph but the added question is itself still too strong; no subsequent resolution is supplied.
worth: Worth recording separately so the author's correction is not mistaken for a correct final theorem; the needed verification is completed here.

title: The third implication of the five-lemma square principle
as_he_states: Beyond the two universal-property implications, he questions whether equivalences at the initial and terminal corners force equivalences at both middle corners of a map of bicartesian squares.
plausible_today: For a coherent morphism of bicartesian squares in a stable derivator, the conclusion holds: the Mayer–Vietoris triangle gives fa⊕fb invertible, hence each component invertible.
state_of_art: GrothPontoShulman2014 Theorem6.1 supplies the exact triangle; P7 independently checks the triangle-isomorphism and block-diagonal steps, including coherence. The source has not stated the stable hypothesis, so the refined theorem is labelled as such.
why_open: The question mark isolates the nonformal implication. No later source says why the author did not finish the argument on this sheet.
worth: High-value commentary item: state the stable proof and hypotheses, avoiding both an unsupported universal assertion and an incorrect blanket refutation.

title: Which localizers satisfy strengthened opposite-edge excision?
as_he_states: W7bis requires each edge of the total-category square of every span to be a W-equivalence exactly when its opposite edge is.
plausible_today: This is an additional condition onW. A sufficient setting is a homotopy-invariant stable coefficient theory that sends the relevant total construction to coherent bicartesian squares and whose isomorphisms detectW. W∞ does not satisfy the reverse implication.
state_of_art: Thomason1979 Theorem1.2 yields standard homotopy-colimit invariance; P8 gives the precise double-cone counterexample to reverse cancellation. Groth2013 Proposition4.5 supplies the stable edge criterion. No classification of all W satisfying the manuscript's strengthened axiom was identified by the recorded label and subject searches.
why_open: The source calls it a strengthened form. Its axiomatic status, rather than a claim about all weak equivalences, is part of the text; no historical abandonment explanation was located.
worth: Worth defining the exact coefficient-detected class and proving only the conditional equivalence; a full classification would require a separate research task.

title: The total/fibre three-condition axiom and its equivalence margin
as_he_states: W8bis proposes two-out-of-three between total equivalence, central-fibre equivalence and equivalence on both branches; the first condition and the margin claiming an equivalence are damaged.
plausible_today: With the first condition read as totalf, standard homotopy-colimit invariance gives b+c⇒a. The other directions require stronger exactness, as supplied in a stable coefficient detection setting. The damaged equivalence to W7 is not reconstructed as a theorem.
state_of_art: P8 checks a+c⇒b fails for W∞ using the explicit acyclic complex. GrothPontoShulman2014 Theorem6.1 supports the coherent stable version. The recorded W7/W8 label searches and primary follow-ups did not identify the exact damaged equivalence.
why_open: The statement and its alleged equivalence are written without proof; uncertain f|fa and cartesian/cofibred wording leave a genuine reading dependency.
worth: Worth a scan-first clarification of the three conditions and map type before treating any asserted W7/W8 equivalence as a research theorem.

title: Smooth/proper corollaries on the final sheet
as_he_states: W7ter/bis and W8ter/bis are called corollaries for smooth total categories overΦ, with a dual proper version; an arrow ofΦ and an edge index are uncertain.
